text:
Pavel Zacha became trade-deadline currency this week, months before the deadline. Several outlets linked him to Minnesota after the Wild missed on Dylan Larkin (Bolavip and NHLTradeRumor.com among them), and Inside The Rink wrote that his market could heat up from here. Causeway Crowd and Heavy both ran pieces on his next contract, which tells you the conversation in Boston has turned to his future.

His present is steady rather than special. Zacha has 18 points in 24 games, half of them on the power play, a pace below last season's 65 points. His own chance creation is down: 0.78 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, from 1.05 last season. The Bruins have also been a little lucky with him on the ice, scoring 4.6 more goals than the chances deserve.

What a buyer would see is in the transition game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries last season and leaving his own zone with possession 64% of the time, both strong for a big center. He has no points in his last two, both Bruins losses.
